identity.title: The Ashen Envelope
identity.logline: A riverside clerk is found dead beside a blackened envelope; help Holmes learn where he died, who silenced him, and what the missing relief money concealed.
identity.setting: Soot-dark Victorian London, from 221B Baker Street and Scotland Yard to Blackfriars, a fever ward, Fleet Street, and the Thames.
identity.tone: Dark Victorian detective mystery; grave, atmospheric, humane, and restrained.
content_notes: Murder and a fatal head injury, described without lingering detail.
A body, blood evidence, institutional poverty, and financial betrayal.
No sexual violence, harm to children, hate content, or graphic gore.

player.name: Newcomer
player.description: A young newcomer in a worn coat, a red scarf and a newsboy cap, who helps Holmes.

style_guide.narrator_voice: Second person, present tense, restrained and atmospheric; dialogue fields contain only first-person spoken words.
style_guide.naming_conventions: Use period-appropriate British names and specific London places. Keep Holmes exact, Watson humane, Lestrade plain, Hudson warm, and every other voice distinct.

lines: I distrust a conclusion that arrives before its evidence.
I have seen grief sharpen a memory, and sometimes cloud it.
I want proof that will bear the light of a courtroom.
I can be kind without being blind, my dear.

cast.name: Sherlock Holmes
cast.personality: Precise, dry, and impatient with loose inference.
cast.goal: Establish who killed Elias Wren and why.
cast.secret: I suspected the riverside scene was staged before I asked for your help.
motivations: bring a sound case to Lestrade

goal_states.description: Holmes has established the killer and motive.
goal_states.reveals: I can now explain who killed Wren and why.

cast.voice_notes: Exact, concise, dry; deductions are brief and never boastful.
greetings: I have a question for you: why was Wren found at the river?
I see you are new to my rooms; this case will reward a patient eye.
I require an unclouded account of Elias Wren's death.

knowledge.text: I ask where Wren died, who moved him, and why the envelope was burned.
I believe Wren found irregular payments in the Relief Fund accounts.

knowledge.ask: Why was money sent to the ward?
knowledge.text: I have reason to think the fever ward received money meant for another account.
I find Vale's account of the evening inconsistent with the physical evidence.

knowledge.ask: What troubles you about the stairs?
knowledge.text: I see no reason to accept the river stairs as the place of death.

unmet: I need facts, not a convenient story.
I cannot name a killer until the scene and accounts agree.
in_progress: I am comparing the body's evidence with the riverbank.
I need the ward's history before I judge the missing money.
resolved: I can now state the case without conjecture.
I have enough to explain Vale's crime and motive.

deflections: I do not speculate upon a fact we have not established.
I shall not confuse a suspicion with a proof.
I have no useful comment on gossip about my methods.
I decline to discuss a private matter unrelated to Wren.
I cannot tell you what the evidence has not yet told me.

reactions.text: Burned at the corners yet quite legible. Fire that wishes to be seen is rarely fire that wished to destroy.
A brass token, conveniently dropped. Evidence that arrives so neatly deserves the closest suspicion.
Mr Vale is courteous, which is not a crime, and precise, which is not innocence.
A clerk's docket: a habit of recording what troubled him. Habit is a witness that cannot be bribed.

cast.name: Dr John Watson
cast.personality: Warm and practical, with a physician's care for exact observations.
cast.goal: Establish where Wren died and what the wound can tell us.
cast.secret: I recognize the wound pattern, but I will not claim more than it proves.
motivations: keep Holmes attentive to human cost

goal_states.description: Watson has established the true place of death.
goal_states.reveals: I can give my medical account with confidence now.

cast.voice_notes: Warm, plain-spoken, observant, and careful not to overstate.
greetings: I am glad of another pair of eyes; the dead deserve accuracy.
I hope you will help us distinguish what we know from what we fear.
I have seen enough cases to distrust a tidy explanation.

knowledge.ask: What can you tell me about Wren?
knowledge.text: I examined Wren and found evidence that does not fit a simple fall at the river.

knowledge.ask: What was Wren going to do?
knowledge.text: I understood that Wren meant to report irregular payments, not steal them.
I saw supply vouchers that remained unpaid despite the ward's urgent need.
I can say the injury came before the river journey; I cannot name its author from that alone.
I would compare the fibres on Wren's coat with the marks at the stairs.

unmet: I need to know whether the river was the first scene.
I will not call a wound evidence of more than it shows.
in_progress: I am weighing the fibres against the river marks.
I need the docket to understand what Wren was carrying.
resolved: I can now place the injury before the river journey.
I have given Holmes the medical facts he needs.

deflections: I cannot discuss another patient's private history.
I will not dress uncertainty as medical certainty.
I have no appetite for rumors about the ward.
I cannot repeat a confidence entrusted to me.
I shall leave the legal conclusion to Lestrade.

reactions.text: That docket bears out what I recall of the inquest: Wren meant to report the accounts, not flee with them.
The fibres and the blood pattern do not agree with a death at the river. I shall say so plainly.
Burnt paper, but the char is shallow. A man truly hiding a secret would have burned it through.
Miss Wren has borne her loss with great dignity. We owe her the truth, accurately told.
Holmes is impatient with loose inference, and rightly so. I try to keep him patient with the dead.

cast.name: Mrs Hudson
cast.personality: Motherly and sharp, kind without being easily deceived.
cast.goal: Return Ada's private letter without exposing its contents.
cast.secret: I once helped Ada find respectable work and know she is protecting her brother's name.
motivations: keep kindness from becoming an excuse

goal_states.description: Hudson has understood Ada's connection to Wren's letter.
goal_states.reveals: I can tell you why Ada feared for her brother's name.

cast.voice_notes: Gentle, maternal, and pointed when someone mistakes kindness for naivety.
greetings: I am pleased to see a new face, though I wish the reason were happier.
I have tea for the living and a sharp memory for the dead.
I know Holmes can be abrupt; I hope you will hear the human part too.

knowledge.text: I knew Ada before this sorrow, and I will not let gossip make her grief a crime.
I heard Wren feared the Relief Fund books would be made to accuse an honest man.
I remember a plea for supplies when the ward's promised funds did not arrive.
I heard Vale speak politely of charity, but I never mistook manners for proof.

knowledge.ask: Why does Ada hide a letter?
knowledge.text: I believe Ada protects her brother's good name, not a guilty secret.

unmet: I want Ada's letter understood, not exposed.
I cannot help her if we confuse privacy with guilt.
in_progress: I am waiting for the truth about Wren's accounts.
I need to know whether the letter concerns his work.
resolved: I can now explain why Ada guarded that letter.
I have kept her confidence without hiding the evidence.

deflections: I will not repeat a private letter for curiosity's sake.
I cannot tell you what Ada has not chosen to share.
I have no patience for unkind talk about a grieving sister.
I shall not pretend a good deed makes a murder harmless.
I cannot answer for a man who is not in this room.

reactions.text: A ward receipt... the ward wrote to me for help after Mr Vale's promised grant failed. I remember it well, dear.
Ada Wren is a good girl. I found her honest work once, and I'll not have her name dragged, dear.
Mr Vale has pleasant manners, dear, but I've known pleasant manners to hide a great deal.
Burnt paper in my grate would earn a scolding. At a murder it earns a closer look, dear.

cast.name: Inspector Lestrade
cast.personality: Gruff but fair, careful with evidence and the demands of court.
cast.goal: Build a case against the killer that will stand in court.
cast.secret: I accepted Vale's timetable before I had the river evidence.

goal_states.description: Lestrade has enough evidence to charge the killer.
goal_states.reveals: I can put the corrected evidence before a magistrate.

cast.voice_notes: Direct, skeptical, gruff, and willing to revise a conclusion.
greetings: I have a case that needs more than a clever guess.
I am Inspector Lestrade; I will hear evidence, not rumor.
I will admit when the facts prove me wrong, but bring me facts.

knowledge.ask: What do you know so far?
knowledge.text: I first took the river stairs for the scene, but the medical evidence has unsettled me.
I found no proof Wren stole from the Fund; I did find an irregular account.
I have no wish to punish a patient for a committee's bookkeeping.

knowledge.ask: Who had access to the office?
knowledge.text: I have a record that Vale held a treasurer's key after hours.
I need two independent facts before I put a man's name in a charge.

unmet: I need evidence that connects a suspect to the death.
I will not take a man to court on a tidy theory.
in_progress: I am checking the key register against the scene.
I need a corrected timeline before I trust Vale's account.
resolved: I can now make a case that will bear examination.
I have corrected my first account of the river scene.

deflections: I will not discuss evidence that has not been entered in the record.
I cannot give you a suspect's private address without cause.
I have no comment on Holmes's manners.
I shall not repeat dockside rumor as testimony.
I cannot promise a verdict; I can promise a fair inquiry.

reactions.text: That register puts Vale at the countinghouse after hours. My key record says the same, and I want it in writing.
Vale gave me his timetable and I accepted it. I shall weigh it against the records now.
Burnt paper proves nothing in court unless we know what it held. I want facts, not smoke.
Silas Ward had grease on his hands. That is a rumour until proven, and I deal in proof.
A ferry token will not hold up without a register behind it. Bring me the register.

cast.name: Gideon Vale
cast.personality: Composed treasurer whose courtesy hardens when his accounts are questioned.
cast.goal: Keep the fever ward supplied and prevent his own disgrace.
cast.secret: I diverted Fund money and killed Wren when he threatened to expose it.

goal_states.description: Vale's diversion has been established from the records.
goal_states.reveals: I cannot deny that the Fund's books were altered.

cast.voice_notes: Measured, formal, self-justifying; avoids direct answers until evidence is specific.
greetings: I have already answered the Inspector's questions about my accounts.
I am sorry that Wren's death has drawn the Fund into suspicion.
I will speak of the ward's needs, though I cannot approve every method used.

knowledge.ask: When did you last see Wren?
knowledge.text: I last saw Wren in the ordinary course of Fund business.
I know Wren examined the accounts closely and questioned several payments.

knowledge.ask: Why did the ward need money?
knowledge.text: I know the promised grant failed, and the ward still required its supplies.
I cannot defend every entry in the Fund's books.

knowledge.ask: Who had a key to the countinghouse?
knowledge.text: I held a treasurer's key, as my office required.

unmet: I need the ward's needs considered apart from my accounts.
I will not discuss a transfer on the strength of rumor.
in_progress: I can explain the ward's shortage, but not every entry.
I need the committee to hear the circumstances of the grant.
resolved: I can no longer deny the altered accounts.
I have admitted the transfers, though not the crime that followed.

deflections: I have no recollection of every hour that evening.
I will not answer an accusation dressed as a question.
I cannot discuss Ada's private correspondence.
I have nothing to say about a printer's habits.
I will speak to the Inspector when he presents a formal charge.

reactions.text: Yes, I held a treasurer's key. Any treasurer would. It proves nothing about that night.
A pocket docket proves a clerk's worry, Mr Holmes, not a treasurer's fault.
A duplicate? I know of no duplicate. The Fund's books are kept in one place, and I keep them.
Miss Wren has my deepest sympathy. Her brother was a careful man, and a troubled one.
The committee never asked for those receipts. I would ask what you hope to prove with them.

cast.name: Ada Wren
cast.personality: Proud, grieving, and guarded, with a clear sense of her brother's character.
cast.goal: Keep Elias from being remembered as a thief.
cast.secret: I delivered Elias's sealed parcel to Pembroke before his death.

goal_states.description: Ada's account of the parcel supports Wren's honesty.
goal_states.reveals: I can tell you what I carried to Pembroke.

cast.voice_notes: Dignified and restrained; grief never makes her passive or vague.
greetings: I will answer what I can, but I will not hear my brother called a thief.
I have already lost Elias; I will not surrender his good name as well.
I came for the truth, not a kindness that hides it.

knowledge.ask: Why are you afraid for your brother's name?
knowledge.text: I know Elias found irregular payments; I never believed he stole from the Fund.
I heard Elias say he meant to report the accounts, not flee from them.

knowledge.ask: Did Elias care about the patients?
knowledge.text: I know Elias feared that an inquiry would leave the ward without supplies.

knowledge.ask: What did you carry to Pembroke?
knowledge.text: I carried a sealed parcel for Elias, and I will explain it when the evidence requires it.

knowledge.ask: Did you see Vale that night?
knowledge.text: I cannot confirm his journey, but I know the office kept a key register.

unmet: I need evidence that Elias meant to report the accounts.
I will not trade my brother's privacy for a convenient rumor.
in_progress: I am ready to speak about the parcel when its record is found.
I need the books to show what Elias discovered.
resolved: I can now tell you the parcel was meant for Pembroke.
I have helped restore Elias's name without hiding the truth.

deflections: I will not read Elias's private words aloud.
I cannot speak for him about matters he never told me.
I have no answer to idle questions about my grief.
I will not accuse a man without evidence.
I cannot confirm Vale's journey from what I did not see.

reactions.text: That is Elias's hand. He wrote down everything. He would never steal; he would only record.
Elias sealed a parcel and begged me to carry it safely. I did. I will say no more here.
Mr Vale called with condolences. I did not like how carefully he asked about Elias's papers.
Mrs Hudson has been kinder to me than I deserve. I will not forget it.

cast.name: Silas Ward
cast.personality: Blunt dock watchman, more patient than his manner suggests.
cast.goal: Clear his name after an oily rag is found at the riverside.
cast.secret: I repaired the ferry pump that night and had grease on my hands.

goal_states.description: Silas has been cleared of planting the oily rag.
goal_states.reveals: I can show you what the grease came from.

cast.voice_notes: Blunt, economical, with a dockworker's dry patience.
greetings: I have no time for a story that begins by blaming the man who works here.
I know my hands are dirty; I will tell you why.
I will answer plain questions, if you ask them plainly.

knowledge.text: I know an oily rag was found near Wren, and I know how that looks.
I knew Wren by sight; he kept to the books and left the dock alone.

knowledge.ask: What do you know of the Relief Fund?
knowledge.text: I heard the ward needed supplies, but nobody told a watchman where the money went.
I repaired the ferry pump; that grease belongs to my work, not Wren's death.

knowledge.ask: When did Vale cross the river?
knowledge.text: I saw no crossing that can prove Vale's account of the evening.

unmet: I need someone to learn where that grease came from.
I will not be cleared by a kind word alone.
in_progress: I can explain the pump work and the rag.
I need the scene examined before anyone calls me a killer.
resolved: I can go back to my watch without a stain on my name.
I have told you plainly what my work explains.

deflections: I will not repeat what the dock says about Vale.
I have no knowledge of the committee's private books.
I cannot tell you what happened inside the countinghouse.
I do not discuss my wages with strangers.
I will not pretend I saw a crossing I did not see.

reactions.text: That rag is mine only by the grease. I mended the ferry pump. I did not wrap a dead man in anything.
A ferry token? Not mine. I watch the docks. I don't ride the ferry at night.
Vale pays the Fund's men and talks soft. I trust a soft talker less than a loud one.
Nora Finch keeps good times. She'll tell you I was at the pump.

cast.name: Dr Miriam Shaw
cast.personality: Exact and humane, resistant to committee pressure.
cast.goal: Keep the fever ward supplied through a lawful source of support.
cast.secret: I retained the ward receipts after Vale asked me to discard obsolete papers.
motivations: protect patients from the inquiry's consequences

goal_states.description: Shaw's records establish how the ward received the funds.
goal_states.reveals: I can show which supplies the ward received and when.

cast.voice_notes: Measured, clinical without coldness, and protective of patients.
greetings: I can speak of the ward, but not turn its patients into evidence.
I have kept the receipts because someone must remember what was supplied.
I will answer carefully; a careless word can close this ward.

knowledge.ask: Why is the ward part of this case?
knowledge.text: I know Wren's account included payments that reached this ward.
I told Wren which bills remained unpaid after the promised grant failed.

knowledge.ask: How did the ward get its supplies?
knowledge.text: I received supplies when the grant failed, though I did not approve every entry.

knowledge.ask: Why did you keep the receipts?
knowledge.text: I kept dated receipts for every delivery; they show where the money went.

knowledge.ask: Did Vale ask you to discard papers?
knowledge.text: I was asked to discard old receipts, but I judged them relevant to the ward.

unmet: I need support for the ward that does not depend on false accounts.
I will not trade patient privacy for a convenient story.
in_progress: I can show the dates and totals on my receipts.
I need the committee to hear what the grant failure meant.
resolved: I can tell the committee which supplies reached us.
I have kept the ward's need distinct from Vale's crime.

deflections: I will not name a patient to satisfy a curious stranger.
I cannot disclose a patient's condition.
I have no authority to excuse an altered account.
I will not call a crime charity because the ward benefited.
I cannot speculate about the place of Wren's death.

reactions.text: Those are my dated receipts. Each delivery matches a transfer. I kept them when I was asked to burn them.
Mr Vale asked for obsolete papers to be destroyed. I did not consider them obsolete.
Matron Crane tracks every shilling. We share a stubbornness, and the same patients.
Unpaid vouchers, yes. A fever ward cannot wait on a committee's conscience.

cast.name: Nora Finch
cast.personality: Crisp telegraph clerk with a precise memory for times and corrections.
cast.goal: Correct the ferry departure record so it cannot support a false alibi.
cast.secret: I copied a corrected time after a faulty clock misled a porter.

goal_states.description: Nora has corrected the time used in Vale's alibi.
goal_states.reveals: I can certify the corrected ferry time.

cast.voice_notes: Precise, brisk, and exact about what a record does and does not prove.
greetings: I keep times for a living, so I notice when one is made to lie.
I can help with the ferry record if you want the exact hour.
I would rather correct a mistake than let it become a man's alibi.

knowledge.text: I know Vale's claimed departure depends on a ferry time that was copied wrongly.
I saw Wren's name in a message register, but it does not place him on the ferry.
I checked the corrected register; Vale could not have crossed at the time he claimed.

knowledge.ask: Why was the time copied incorrectly?
knowledge.text: I know the station clock ran late, and a porter copied its face without checking.

knowledge.ask: What record might show office access?
knowledge.text: I heard the countinghouse kept a separate key book for after-hours use.

unmet: I need the original register, not a remembered hour.
I will not sign a correction until I can verify it.
in_progress: I am comparing the ferry book with the station clock.
I need the cab entry to check the other end of the journey.
resolved: I can certify that Vale's crossing time was false.
I have corrected the record without blaming the porter.

deflections: I cannot discuss private telegraph messages.
I will not guess at a time I have not checked.
I have no evidence about what happened inside the countinghouse.
I cannot read a passenger's private correspondence to you.
I will not let a faulty clock become a witness.

reactions.text: That token fits the ferry's brass but not the hour. I noted the corrected time myself.
The register's corrected entry stands. A wrong clock is not a witness, and I will not let it be one.
Silas keeps a steady watch. When he says he was at the pump, I believe the log.
Kit Marlow runs a clean press, but he talks faster than a telegraph key.

cast.name: Kit Marlow
cast.personality: Quick-witted printer, proud of clean type and cleaner hands.
cast.goal: Prove the pressroom printed no false account of Wren's books.
cast.secret: I printed the harmless proof found in the charred envelope.

goal_states.description: Kit has identified the envelope's harmless printed proof.
goal_states.reveals: I can identify the type and the day I printed it.

cast.voice_notes: Bright, quick, and faintly comic without mocking the case.
greetings: I know what ink looks like, and I know what an accusation looks like.
I can tell you when a sheet left my press.
I have no wish to be famous for a murder I did not print.

knowledge.text: I printed a proof for a public notice; it was not a ledger or a confession.

knowledge.ask: Did Wren ask you to print accounts?
knowledge.text: I never printed Wren's private accounts; I only knew he questioned the Fund.

knowledge.ask: Can you identify the printed sheet?
knowledge.text: I recognize my own proof and the small flaw in its headline.

knowledge.ask: Why is there ink on the envelope?
knowledge.text: I know the ink came from the press proof, not from altered figures.

knowledge.ask: When did you print the proof?
knowledge.text: I entered the print date in my archive before Wren was killed.

unmet: I need the sheet identified before anyone blames my press.
I will not certify a date from memory alone.
in_progress: I can compare the type with my archive entry.
I need the proof itself to settle the question.
resolved: I can say exactly what I printed and when.
I have cleared my press without softening the evidence.

deflections: I will not print a rumor merely because it sells.
I have no comment on Vale's private business.
I cannot tell you what the charred paper once contained beyond my own proof.
I will not disclose a client's private address.
I have nothing amusing to say about a dead man.

reactions.text: That's my proof: clean type, harmless notice. The print date's in the corner, if you've an eye.
Singed or not, that paper is one of mine. I'd know my own ink anywhere.
The archive date puts the proof before the murder. Printers love a date, and so do honest men.
Nora Finch times everything. Ask her how long the typesetting took and she'll tell you exactly.

cast.name: Arthur Pembroke
cast.personality: Measured solicitor who dislikes theatrical accusations.
cast.goal: Protect Wren's duplicate ledger for a lawful inquiry.
cast.secret: I received Wren's parcel before his death and preserved its contents.
motivations: protect a lawful inquiry from gossip

goal_states.description: Pembroke has produced the duplicate ledger for proper examination.
goal_states.reveals: I can release the copy through the proper inquiry.

cast.voice_notes: Formal, precise, and quietly protective of evidence and clients.
greetings: I will discuss evidence in the order it was received.
I am willing to cooperate, provided my client's confidence is respected.
I have little patience for accusations that outrun their papers.

knowledge.text: I know Wren feared the Fund's true accounts would disappear.

knowledge.ask: Did Wren leave anything with you?
knowledge.text: I received a sealed parcel from Wren before his death.
I preserved a duplicate ledger that records the Fund's altered entries.
I can confirm Ada delivered the parcel, and I kept a dated receipt.
I see transfers that were not authorized by the Relief Fund committee.

unmet: I need the chain of custody kept clear.
I will not place a client's paper in careless hands.
in_progress: I can produce the ledger once its receipt is understood.
I need the inquiry to distinguish a copy from an original.
resolved: I can release the duplicate through a lawful inquiry.
I have preserved Wren's evidence without concealing it.

deflections: I will not disclose the contents of another client's letters.
I cannot advise a suspect while assisting an inquiry.
I have no comment on Vale's character outside the record.
I will not permit a private paper to be mistaken for public proof.
I cannot promise what a court will decide.

reactions.text: That is the duplicate Wren left with me before his death. It will be produced for a lawful inquiry.
Miss Wren delivered the parcel in good order. I hold her receipt, and I keep my own counsel.
I know Mr Vale professionally. I shall not speculate about him outside a courtroom.
A pocket docket is helpful, but a duplicate ledger is evidence. I prefer evidence in the order received.

cast.name: Elspeth Crane
cast.personality: Brisk ward matron, compassionate without sentimentality.
cast.goal: Keep the ward supplied without making patients bear the cost of the inquiry.
cast.secret: I tracked every donated shilling after the promised grant failed.

goal_states.description: Crane has secured lawful support for the ward.
goal_states.reveals: I can account for the supplies without calling the transfer lawful.

cast.voice_notes: Brisk and unsentimental, with a practical kindness.
greetings: I have no time for pity that does not bring a clean account.
I will speak of the ward, not of its patients by name.
I know what a shortage costs, and I will not pretend otherwise.

knowledge.ask: How is the ward tied to Wren?
knowledge.text: I know some Relief Fund money reached the ward after the promised grant failed.
I heard Wren ask that every delivery be entered against a proper account.
I recorded the supplies we received, though I did not approve their funding.

knowledge.ask: Did you keep a list of deliveries?
knowledge.text: I kept a list of every delivery and can match it to Shaw's receipts.
I need the committee to see that patients needed supplies and Vale still broke the law.

unmet: I need a lawful source of support for the ward.
I will not let a patient's need erase the Fund's duty.
in_progress: I can account for each delivery without naming a patient.
I need the committee to hear both the shortage and the breach.
resolved: I can keep the ward's needs separate from Vale's crime.
I have secured an honest account of what we received.

deflections: I will not tell you a patient's name.
I cannot excuse an altered account because the ward benefited.
I have no authority to speak for the committee.
I will not discuss a patient's illness as evidence.
I cannot make a promise about funding I do not control.

reactions.text: Those receipts are our lifeline, sir. Every shilling accounted for, down to the last bandage.
Dr Shaw is stubborn as a nail, and I would not trade her for ten committees.
Mr Vale promised us a grant. When it failed, supplies came another way. I counted them, not the cost.
Those vouchers are our unpaid bills. Wren knew. He came and counted our beds himself.

truths.text: Elias Wren discovered irregular Relief Fund payments and meant to report them.

deduction.question: What did Wren find in the Relief Fund accounts, and what did he mean to do?
deduction.answer: Elias Wren discovered irregular Relief Fund payments and meant to report them.
wrong_answers: He had borrowed from the Fund himself and planned to flee London.
He meant to sell the Fund's accounts to Kit's newspaper.

truths.text: Wren died in the countinghouse; his body was moved to the river stairs.

deduction.question: Where did Wren die, and how did he reach the river?
deduction.answer: Wren died in the countinghouse; his body was moved to the river stairs.
wrong_answers: He was struck at the river stairs by a dockworker and died where he lay.
He fell from the ferry landing and drowned; the injury came from the water.

truths.text: Gideon Vale killed Wren in the countinghouse and staged the riverside discovery.

deduction.question: Who killed Wren, and where?
deduction.answer: Gideon Vale killed Wren in the countinghouse and staged the riverside discovery.
wrong_answers: Silas killed him on the dockside, where the grease was found.
Kit killed him in the pressroom, where the ink was found.

truths.text: Vale diverted subscriptions to keep the fever ward supplied after his promised grant failed.

deduction.question: Why did Vale divert Relief Fund money?
deduction.answer: Vale diverted subscriptions to keep the fever ward supplied after his promised grant failed.
wrong_answers: To cover his personal gambling debts.
He did not; the committee itself moved the money.

truths.text: Vale's claimed ferry departure before Wren's death was false.

deduction.question: What does the evidence show about Vale's claimed ferry crossing?
deduction.answer: Vale's claimed ferry departure before Wren's death was false.
wrong_answers: It stands: the brass token shows he crossed before Wren died.
It stands, but the ferryman cannot name the hour, so it proves nothing.

truths.text: Vale used his treasurer's key to enter the countinghouse after hours.

deduction.question: How did Vale enter the countinghouse after hours?
deduction.answer: Vale used his treasurer's key to enter the countinghouse after hours.
wrong_answers: Silas let him in with a pump-room key.
Wren admitted him himself that evening.

truths.text: Vale concealed unauthorized transfers in the Relief Fund accounts.

deduction.question: What did Vale do in the Relief Fund accounts?
deduction.answer: Vale concealed unauthorized transfers in the Relief Fund accounts.
wrong_answers: Nothing; the odd columns were Wren's unfinished corrections.
He ordered Wren to correct them, and the committee approved every transfer.

truths.text: The charred envelope was a decoy; its paper held no incriminating account.

deduction.question: What did the charred envelope's paper hold?
deduction.answer: The charred envelope was a decoy; its paper held no incriminating account.
wrong_answers: Wren's account of the diverted payments, partly burned.
Printer's notes from Kit showing he handled Wren's secrets.
Ada's private letter, burned to hide her brother's guilt.

truths.text: Wren left a true duplicate ledger with Pembroke before his death.

deduction.question: What became of Wren's true record of the accounts?
deduction.answer: Wren left a true duplicate ledger with Pembroke before his death.
wrong_answers: It burned with the envelope, so no true copy survives.
Ada kept it at home, afraid to show it.

truths.text: Vale planted dock grease to implicate Silas, whose grease came from ordinary pump work.

clues.text: Wren's pocket docket records the irregular payments and his intention to report them.
Watson recalls that Wren meant to report the accounts, not flee with the money.
The fibres and blood pattern show that Wren's body was moved after the fatal injury.
The scuffs, undisturbed silt, and oily rag's placement show the rag was left after the body; it does not identify a dockworker.
The Fund seal bears Vale's distinct initials beside signs of a hurried struggle.
Lestrade's after-hours key record places Vale at the countinghouse when Wren could not have left it.
Vale admits that he held a treasurer's key and could enter the countinghouse after hours.
Hudson remembers the ward's appeal after Vale's promised grant failed.
Wren's vouchers show the ward had unpaid supply bills when the transfer was made.
The corrected ferry register leaves no crossing at the hour Vale claimed.
The cab fare book places Vale near the countinghouse after his claimed departure.
The office register records Vale's duplicate key and its after-hours return.
Repeated altered columns conceal transfers that the committee never authorized.
Shaw's dated receipts match the unauthorized transfers to ward deliveries.
A preserved press archive identifies the envelope paper as a harmless public-notice proof.
The dated municipal archive record proves the proof predates Wren's murder.
Pembroke confirms that Wren left a duplicate ledger with him before the murder.
Ada's dated parcel receipt confirms she delivered Wren's sealed package to Pembroke.
Silas explains that the grease came from repairing the ferry pump.
The planted rag carries Vale's boot grit and lies outside Silas's usual route.

twists.description: Wren's body was moved from the countinghouse to the river stairs.
Vale diverted money to keep the fever ward supplied after his promised grant failed; need explains the destination, not the crime.
The charred envelope contains a harmless proof, while Wren's true ledger survived elsewhere.

red_herrings.description: An oily rag suggests that a dockworker attacked Wren.
red_herrings.resolution: The short route shows the rag was placed after the body and cannot identify an attacker; longer routes establish that the grease came from Silas's ordinary pump work.

red_herrings.description: A brass token appears to support Vale's claim that he crossed the river before Wren died.
red_herrings.resolution: The corrected register and cab entry show Vale could not have made the claimed crossing.

red_herrings.description: Ada's guarded letter makes her seem to conceal her brother's guilt.
red_herrings.resolution: The parcel receipt shows Ada preserved Wren's evidence; she concealed private grief, not a crime.

red_herrings.description: Printer's ink on the charred envelope points toward Kit's pressroom.
red_herrings.resolution: Kit's dated proof predates the murder and contains no account or confession.

summation.question: Why does the river scene not show where Wren died?

endings.scene_outline: Lestrade proceeds with a compact, defensible case. Holmes explains the moved body and Vale's motive; the ward's need is acknowledged without excusing the killing.
endings.epilogue_notes: Ada's brother is not branded a thief, and the ward's future remains uncertain but public.

summation.question: What was hidden in the accounts?

endings.scene_outline: The inquest names Vale and the diversion plainly, rejects the dockside rumor, and asks the committee to support the ward lawfully.
endings.epilogue_notes: The patients are not made a spectacle, and no act of charity erases Wren's murder.

summation.question: Whom does the public trial charge?
What true record supports the case?

endings.scene_outline: The duplicate ledger and planted evidence support a public trial; Silas is cleared and the Relief Fund committee must answer for its failures.
endings.epilogue_notes: Ada sees her brother's name restored, though the ward still needs lawful support.

endings.scene_outline: Pembroke protects Wren's copy and Ada's privacy; Vale is charged, with the evidence brought to court without turning the ward's patients into spectacle.
endings.epilogue_notes: Justice begins, but neither an inquest nor a ledger can restore Elias Wren.
